label: Bupivacaine — systemic disposition + site absorption

parameters.label: apparent volume of distribution (reference adult)
parameters.covariate_model: reference-adult disposition (no covariate model in LA0; ~1.0 L/kg)

extraction.tier_rationale: Standard reference-adult LA disposition value (Tier-C by design). Bupivacaine is long-acting and the most cardiotoxic common amide; the cardiotoxicity differentiation is v0.6 LA2.
extraction.source_locator: Tucker & Mather 1979; standard LA PK reference values

parameters.label: systemic clearance (reference adult)
parameters.covariate_model: reference-adult disposition (no covariate model in LA0)

extraction.source_locator: Tucker & Mather 1979; standard LA PK reference values

extraction.tier_rationale: Site-absorption rank order robust; absolute ka Tier-C, applied site-wise (the site dominates the rate of rise). The narrower cardiovascular margin of bupivacaine vs ropivacaine at similar block is the v0.6 LA2 educational comparison.

toxicity_thresholds.method_caveat: Volunteer slow i.v. infusion (Knudsen 1997); CNS symptoms (circumoral numbness, tinnitus, light-headedness) at ~2 ug/mL total mean. Speed of rise and acidosis lower the threshold — a rapid intravascular injection is NOT this slow-infusion number.
toxicity_thresholds.saturation_caveat: Bupivacaine binding SATURATES: at high total concentration the free (toxic) fraction rises non-linearly, so this total-basis range UNDER-predicts free-drug risk exactly when total is highest. Compare against the free-basis threshold below.

toxicity_thresholds.method_caveat: Free (unbound) plasma concentration at first CNS symptoms (Knudsen 1997). The free-basis companion to the total-basis range above — toxicity tracks FREE drug, so this is the more mechanistically faithful threshold.

Bupivacaine is the most CARDIOTOXIC common amide (fast-in/slow-out avid cardiac Na-channel binding): the cardiovascular margin OVER the CNS-warning range is narrow or absent — arrhythmia/arrest can occur with little or no CNS prodrome, unlike less cardiotoxic agents. The agent-choice differentiation (vs ropivacaine/levobupivacaine) is v0.6 LA2.
toxicity_thresholds.saturation_caveat: Saturable binding: this total-basis cardiovascular range under-predicts free-drug risk at high total concentration (v0.6 LA3).

extraction.tier_rationale: Cardiovascular threshold ranges are wide, method-dependent and ethically un-doseable in volunteers; Tier-C by construction. The clinically load-bearing fact is the NARROW CNS-to-CVS margin, not a precise number.
extraction.source_locator: Knudsen 1997; Scott 1989 (acute toxicity, bupivacaine vs ropivacaine)

extraction.tier_rationale: v0.6 LA0: systemic disposition + site absorption only — no toxicity thresholds (LA1). Site-of-injection dominance is the headline. Disposition + ka Tier-C; the site rank is the robust claim.
extraction.source_locator: Tucker & Mather 1979; standard LA PK reference values

source_review.reviewed_by: automated source cross-check (Claude Opus 4.8 via Hypnos research agents)
source_review.method: fetched FDA/EMA labels (DailyMed/SmPC), primary-paper PubMed abstracts, open implementations, and CrossRef, then compared each curated value against the fetched values
source_review.notes: Vdss 73 L is an EXACT match to the bupivacaine SmPC. Total clearance: curated 0.47 L/min vs SmPC 0.58 L/min (~19% lower) — the curated value is a plausible disposition estimate but below the labelled racemate clearance. HUMAN ITEM: reconcile CL against the primary Tucker & Mather 1979 table (paywalled, not directly read).

notes: Systemic concentration only. Saturable protein binding (free fraction rises non-linearly at high total concentration) is curated on the drug record and surfaced as the LA3 failure mode; cardiotoxicity differentiation vs ropivacaine is LA2.
